posts.title: What Dawkins, Graham and Hickey Agree On
posts.description: One of the most underrated skills is refusing to tie your identity to an idea. The moment an idea becomes part of who you are, you stop evaluating it and start defending it. You become its servant. Richard Dawkins called these “viruses of the mind”: ideas that spread and persist not because they’re true, but because they’re good at protecting themselves.
